chunks: I swear by Allah that, had it not been for (my) giving you time, you would have faced from me catastrophe that would have crushed the bones and removed the flesh!

key_terms.تَهْلِسُ: To remove / to strip off (specifically flesh from bone)
key_terms.قَوَارِعُ: Catastrophes / severe blows / things that strike suddenly

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean by 'qawari' (catastrophes/blows) in his letter to Muawiya?
ai.summary: In this vivid metaphor from his letter to Muawiya, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts his latent military power with his strategic patience, using the imagery of 'qawari' (heavy maces) to signify decisive, crushing force. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *hilm* (forbearance) not as weakness, but as a calculated restraint to preserve the community or await the right moment for justice. The phrase underscores the tension between immediate retribution and the wisdom of delayed action in political and spiritual leadership.
